html:
Sholay is a 1975 Hindi action film made in Bombay, directed by Ramesh Sippy and written by Salim and Javed. It became one of the most watched and most quoted films in India.

Two small time crooks, Jai and Veeru, played by Amitabh Bachchan and Dharmendra, are hired by a former police officer to catch the bandit Gabbar Singh, who has terrorised a village. The story borrows from Hollywood westerns and from Seven Samurai, set in the rocky country of the Deccan.

It opened on 15 August 1975, weeks into the Emergency, and the censors made the makers change the ending so that the police, not the hero, deal with the villain. Reviews were cool at first, but word of mouth made it a hit; it ran at one Bombay cinema for five years. Gabbar's lines passed into everyday speech, and the film helped make Bachchan the angry young man of Hindi cinema in the 1970s.
sum: Sholay is a 1975 Hindi action film made in Bombay, directed by Ramesh Sippy and written by Salim and Javed. It became one of the most watched and most quoted films in India.
